PS: Are there any possibilities in lavaan to include the 'age' variable as a spline, for example, using the methodology from Song, XY and Lu, ZH and Cai, JH and Ip, EHS (2013): 'A Bayesian modeling approach for generalized semiparametric structural equation models'  or something similar?

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Quadratic (or non-linear) Regression Term
parts:
The un standardized parameter estimates and standard errors for age squared are small partly because the variance of age squared is so large, relative to that of the dependent variable.  (The standard errors are not 0, but they are scaled a few decimal places to the left.)  If you have a doubt, run the model without the squared terms, and compare the R2 for the factors from that model with the R2 here.  The increment in R2 will tell you if the squared term is making a practically significant contribution.
--Ed Rigdon

parts:
Regarding to your model, it is a little complicated in computing the df because your model has exogenous variables. It involves the matrices of predicting items by age and age2 and latent variables by age and age2. 

To answer your question, it is simpler to consider the model without age and age2, which would be as follows:

N =~ N1+N2+N3+N4+N5+N6
     E =~ E1+E2+E3+E4+E5+E6
     O =~ O1+O2+O3+O4+O5+O6
     A =~ A1+A2+A3+A4+A5+A6
     C =~ C1+C2+C3+C4+C5+C6

Then, you may use this model to try to calculate df. You will get a big number. See the following book in pp. 65-67:

http://books.google.com/books?id=QTasbvQCZQcC&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false

The change in R2 is an effect size index. The likelihood-ratio test is the null hypothesis testing of b = 0. Like in multiple regression, you need to check both t-test and the change in R2.
